title: Registered Limit of Liability: Valuation of the Covered Item on a Northgate Protect Single-Item Plan
content:
**Valuation clause.** On a Northgate Protect single-item plan, the covered order line is the order line named on the plan, and the covered order is the order named on the plan. The registered limit of liability is the covered item price recorded on the plan, rounded half up to the cent.

**Assembly of the figure.** The registered limit is built on its starting price, which is settled before anything else; every amount that comes off the registered limit or is added to it is applied to that starting price, and the registered limit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end, never at an intermediate point.

## Inputs

| Quantity | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Covered order line | The order line named on the plan |
| Covered order | The order named on the plan |
| Covered item price | The price recorded on the plan for the covered item, the net price paid for it before tax |

## Worked example on hypothetical figures

A plan records a covered item price of $618.40 for the order line it names. The registered limit of liability is $618.40. Had the recorded price carried a fraction of a cent, for instance $618.405 in a hypothetical, the figure would be rounded half up once, to $618.41.

## Points of judgement

- The figure belongs to the covered order line the plan names, not to any other line of the same order.
- Rounding is half up to the cent and happens a single time, after the figure is complete.
